entries.notes: Parking payments, which is part of driving, so it sits beside Pango. No policy: nobody has measured which hosts it needs, and a host list invented for it would be a guess wearing the clothes of a rule.

Israeli weather forecasts. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.24, versionCode 94), signed with the developer's own key (CN=111111). It is a WebViewActivity around the mobile site, m.weather2day.co.il, with AdMob on top: banners, interstitials, rewarded and native ads, which carry pictures. The policy blocks the ad hosts; see it for what it cannot reach.

Installed from the latest GitHub release. sha256 computed with apksigner from Mailtice-1.6.0.apk (versionCode 12), single signer CN=Mailtice, O=abaye123. Network in every mode that has network at all, with no host policy.

Installed from the latest GitHub release. Two accepted signers: e1d3... is the Play App Signing certificate of the copy from Google Play (computed with apksigner from the copy on the reference device, versionCode 1), and 2d5f... is the developer's own certificate on the GitHub APK (MusicRadio-1.0.12.apk, versionCode 20, CN=abaye, OU=MusicRadio). The two are not interchangeable on one device: a Play copy cannot be updated in place by the GitHub APK.

Shared scooters. Flagged hasUnmodestImage: the sign in screen plays a video of people riding (res/raw/intro_video.mp4), packaged in the APK, so the tunnel cannot remove it. Braze, Stripe, Braintree and PayPal, Persona for identity checks, Zendesk. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (4.421.0.1, versionCode 908560), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Bird Ride, O=Bird Rides, L=Santa Monica, ST=CA, C=01). The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Not published on Play, so it is not offered for installation and is installed by hand. The entry exists because network access is decided here: a package that is not in the catalog gets nothing, whatever its policy says. Two certificates are accepted while this app is still in development: the release key (C=IL, O=abaye, CN=abaye) and the debug key of the machine it is built on (C=US, O=Android, CN=Android Debug), which is what is installed on the test device today. Drop the debug entry once the app ships.

The package name is com.alert.meserhadash, not the com.ioref.meserhadashtv that KDroidDatabase files this under. The certificate settles it: the application installed on the test device carries SHA-1 131c243751d9ea44299c0a97311deee77eb2345e, which is exactly the value upstream records for that other name. Same signer, different package name, and only this one exists on a phone. minUserMode is NAVIGATION_ONLY, the lowest mode in which anything reaches the internet at all, because an alert application that cannot reach its server is worse than absent: the device looks protected and is not.

Hiking and offroad maps. Flutter, Mapbox and MapLibre, Firebase and the Facebook SDK. Flagged hasUnmodestImage, like Israel Hiking Map: points of interest carry photos users upload. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.4.3, versionCode 2004031), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Yoav Rofe, OU=Amud Anan, O=Amud Anan, L=Jerusalem, ST=Jerusalem, C=IL). The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Granted network on the assumption that it is a service client. If it turns out to work offline this should become false: network here is opt-in, and an application that does not need it should not have it.

Opening gates and barriers by phone. Its network security configuration names api1.pal-es.com and that is all it reached. Firebase and Google Maps. No ad SDK. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Most of the host list extract_hosts.py prints for it is the public suffix list bundled in a library, not hosts it reaches. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.6.0076, versionCode 447), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Nisso Pardo, OU=Developer, O=Pal-Electronics, L=Ranana, ST=Israel, C=972).

Parking payment. React Native, Google Maps, Firebase and AppsFlyer. No ad SDK. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.2.0, versionCode 309), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).

Podcasts and shiurim. It carries video: a YouTube and Vimeo player and VAST video ads (go.aniview.com, Google IMA). Flagged hasUnmodestImage because episode artwork and video come from the server and cannot be known in advance. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.9.8, versionCode 20908), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Afcon EV charging, on the Driivz platform. It reached mobile.afconev.co.il only. Payment SDKs (Stripe, Adyen, Braintree), Google Maps, Firebase. No ad SDK. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (9.1.23-a691ee5218, versionCode 27252), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).

Sonol EVI EV charging, on the Driivz platform. It reached mobile.sonolevi.co.il only. Payment SDKs (Stripe, Adyen, Braintree), Google Maps, Firebase. No ad SDK. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (9.1.20-9302ab832e, versionCode 27237), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Joseph Levy, O=Driivz LTD, C=IL).

Public transport, so it sits at NAVIGATION_ONLY beside the train and Moovit. KDroidDatabase has no policy for this package, and none is written here either: with no policy an allowed application is FULL_OPEN inside the tunnel, which is the honest state for a timetable and ticketing application nobody has measured. The certificate was read off the build installed on the test device.

Map of springs. A Capacitor web application backed by Supabase (sbnbfpihfhsyctumpqod.supabase.co), with Leaflet maps from MapTiler, OpenStreetMap and govmap. No ad SDK and no analytics. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Flagged hasUnmodestImage: spring photos come from upload.wikimedia.org and from users, and a photo of a spring may show bathers. Blocking the photo hosts was considered and left out for now. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.0.0, versionCode 11), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Two factor codes. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (7.2, versionCode 7002011), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). No policy, so it is fully open inside the tunnel, by choice. The codes themselves are computed on the device and need no network; the network is for backing the accounts up to the Google account and restoring them. Available from NAVIGATION_ONLY because a device in the strictest modes still has to sign in to things, and it shows nothing but codes.
Preinstalled on the test device, so it is granted network but not offered for installation. Signature pinned from that device.

A file manager for the device's own storage. Pin and version from the build installed from Play on the F21 Pro (1.9291, versionCode 1593359), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). No network on purpose: browsing, opening, moving and cleaning up files all work offline, and what the network adds (cloud backup, cleaning suggestions) is not needed. It holds REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES and can open an APK it finds on the storage; whether that installs is decided by the install restrictions on the device, not by this entry. Nearby Share goes over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi Direct, which the Bluetooth sharing restriction governs.

Pin and version from the build installed from Play (9.27.28, versionCode 700328882), signed with Google's own key (CN=Unknown, OU=Google, Inc), not Play App Signing. No policy, so it is fully open inside the tunnel, by choice. Everything it does runs through Google hosts it cannot work without (translate-pa.googleapis.com, translate.google.com, inputtools.google.com, www.gstatic.com), so a blocklist would have nothing useful to name. No ad SDK. Translating a website goes through a *.translate.goog proxy, which can stand in for any site; the application hands that to the browser rather than showing it itself, so it is the browser's network that decides whether it loads. Camera translation shows what the camera sees, not images from the web.
Needed for spoken navigation directions

Drivers' application from grivo.co.il. React Native, Mapbox and Google Maps, Firebase, Facebook SDK, LogRocket and Microsoft Clarity. No ad unit found. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.8.6, versionCode 4194916), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).

Hebrew speech to text, with voice destination search in Waze. Listed on Ogen Play, whose downloads need a sign in and hand out a signed link that expires after five minutes, so it cannot be a source. The application's own updater names a public repository instead, o054840/hebvoice-updates, and its latest release asset (HebrewVoice-v3.9.2.apk, versionCode 25) is byte for byte the Ogen Play file: sha256 55981e59...6253 on both, and the same value in the repository's update.json. Signed with the developer's own key (CN=HebrewVoice, O=Private, C=IL). The in-app updater installs from the same repository, and only a build signed with this key can update it in place.
Kol Halashon's older native player (2.67, versionCode 267, from Play), signed by Kol Halashon, the same key as com.khl.www2. A native player, unlike the WebView of com.khl.www2; see the policy notes.
Kol Halashon's current application (2.10, versionCode 20100, from Play), signed by Kol Halashon, the same key as com.khl.kiosk. A WebView over www.kolhalashon.com.

Libra insurance's CHIK. React Native, Firebase, Facebook SDK and AppsFlyer. No ad SDK. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.1.4, versionCode 20), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).

Shared scooters. No video is packaged in the APK; the test did not get past the splash screen, so the screens after it were not seen. Braze, Branch, Amplitude, Datadog, Mapbox, Stripe and Braintree. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.288.0, versionCode 3288000), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Lime Bike, OU=Mobile Development, O=LimeBike, L=San Mateo, ST=California, C=US).

Was APKPURE, but apkpure.com answers 410 Gone for this package, and APKCOMBO was never a source the store could download from. Now PLAY. The pin was taken from the APKCombo build, which mirrors the Play release and carries the same certificate.

Ministry of Transport parking application, so it sits beside Pango and Cellopark. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.1.1, versionCode 113), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). It is an OutSystems shell: the screens are a web application served from transportation.outsystems.app and shown in a WebView. No policy, so it is fully open inside the tunnel, by choice. An allow list of that one host was written and dropped: the WebView's content security policy also permits *.amazonaws.com, which in OutSystems usually means uploads to presigned S3 URLs whose host is only known at runtime, and a list that misses it breaks those screens without saying why.
Off road route navigation. Granted network because its maps and tracks come from a server; no policy, for the same reason as Cellopark.

Granted network. I had it offline on the reasoning that a star map draws the sky from a catalogue and a clock, which is true of the drawing and not of everything else it does: the free build fetches its extended catalogues, satellite elements and imagery on demand, and without the network those simply never appear. Network is opt-in in this catalog, so the default was the safe direction; being wrong in that direction costs a feature that silently does nothing, which is worse to diagnose than a refusal.

Driving theory test practice. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (15.0.0, versionCode 92), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Erez, C=IL). It carries real advertising: AdMob with nineteen ad units (banners, interstitials, rewarded), Facebook Audience Network and ironSource mediation, plus a local ad server, deliver.trustmedia.co.il. The policy blocks all of them; see it for what that costs.

Loading the Rav-Kav card over NFC. A Cordova application that reaches ravkavonline.co.il and Google Maps. No ad SDK. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.17.2, versionCode 24001702), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Pcentra, OU=Pcentra, O=Pcentra, L=Israel, ST=Israel, C=IL).

Reads a licence plate and looks the vehicle up, so without network it does nothing at all. The signing certificate is Google's, not the developer's (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.), because the application is distributed through Play App Signing; that is the certificate an installed copy carries and therefore the one to pin.

Alerts, so it is granted network and sits at the lowest mode in which anything reaches the internet at all. Its certificate SHA-1 is exactly the value KDroidDatabase records for this package, so the build on the device is the build its policy was written for. The application calls itself Tzofar on the launcher; the name here is the one people ask for.

Samsung Weather, preinstalled on the test device at /system/app/SamsungWeather/SamsungWeather.apk, so it is granted network but not offered for installation. Signature pinned from that device. Category is TOOLS rather than SYSTEM on purpose: CatalogMapper exempts SYSTEM entries from the sha256 validity gate, and this entry has a real pin that should be enforced.

Siddur from Siddurim.com, the same code base as Siddur Klilat Yofi under a different key. No ad SDK; Firebase for sync, remote config and Crashlytics. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.5.4, versionCode 899), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).

Siddur, nusach Ashkenaz, from Siddurim.com; the same code as the Sfard build and the same signing key. No ad SDK; Firebase for sync, remote config and Crashlytics. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.5.4, versionCode 899), signed with the developer's own key (O=Siddurim.com).

Siddur, nusach Sfard, from Siddurim.com. No ad SDK; Firebase for sync, remote config and Crashlytics. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.5.4, versionCode 899), signed with the developer's own key (O=Siddurim.com).

Sonol fuelling. React Native, Google Maps, Firebase, Branch, Sentry and Forter. No ad SDK. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.7.4, versionCode 30000030), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Sonol, OU=Sonol, O=Sonol, L=Israel, ST=Israel, C=IL).
Play delivers this as a base APK plus configuration splits (~169 MB in all). The pin is the certificate of the BASE apk, which is the only member PackageManager reports for the package.

EV charger map. It carries advertising (Google Ad Manager, AdMob, Amazon Publisher Services, PubMatic), all blocked by its policy. Braze, Amplitude, OneTrust, Stripe. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (4.52.0, versionCode 20402), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Unknown, OU=Unknown, O=Unknown, L=Unknown, ST=Unknown, C=Unknown).

Gnrgy EV charging. It reached portal.gnrgy.com only. Google Maps and Firebase. No ad SDK. No policy, so it is open inside the tunnel. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (8.8, versionCode 724), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Midhun Madhu, OU=Software Department, O=Gnrgy, L=Bangalore, ST=Karnataka, C=IN).

Routes for kohanim that avoid cemeteries, the same need Derech Kohanim answers. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (15.1, versionCode 15), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). No policy, so it is fully open inside the tunnel, by choice. It is a Capacitor web application with a MapLibre map; its network security configuration names gps.hakohanim.org, api.maptiler.com, tile.openstreetmap.org, server.arcgisonline.com, nominatim.openstreetmap.org and unpkg.com, and the code also reaches tiles.openfreemap.org and photon.komoot.io. No ad SDK and no analytics were found.

Finds a grave and walks you to it inside the cemetery. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.2.5, versionCode 104), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). No advertising: none of the common ad SDKs are in the dex, the Google Ads classes present are the ones Firebase Analytics pulls in, and there is no AdMob application id. The 'AdvertisementService' class is Bluetooth LE advertising, not ads. sonol.co.il and trail-camera.co.il are website tags on points in the bundled OpenStreetMap extracts, and hagilda.com is a font's copyright line.

The Ten fuel station chain: fuelling, prices, coupons. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (3.8, versionCode 80), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). Flagged hasUnmodestImage: it shows its own promotional banners and coupons (BannerView, FeedBanner, AppBanner in the dex), sometimes with a woman in the picture. They come from the same server as the rest of the application, ten.inmanage.com, with image URLs handed out at runtime, so no host rule can take the banners out and leave the fuelling working. The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance before it is installed or gets network. No third party ad SDK and no AdMob application id.
Looks a permit up in a government register, which is the whole of what it does, so without network it does nothing at all.

Paz fuelling and Yellow club. Flagged hasUnmodestImage: the home screen and What's New show marketing images and stories served by Paz, which change without a release. AppsFlyer, Emarsys, Facebook SDK, New Relic. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (8.13.0.1344, versionCode 1344), signed with the developer's own key (CN=Paz Oil, O=Paz Oil Company Ltd, C=IL). The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Hiking and trail maps on OpenStreetMap, open source. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (9.21.256, versionCode 921256), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.). No ad SDK. Flagged hasUnmodestImage: points of interest show photos from Wikimedia Commons, iNature and pictures users upload to the project's own server, mostly landscapes but open to anyone, so what appears cannot be known in advance. The flag keeps it out of REDUCED_RISK and asks for explicit acceptance; MOST_OPEN is stated so the entry says what the flag already means.

Yedidim volunteer roadside assistance: calls for help and volunteer dispatch, with background location. Flutter, Google Maps, Firebase, Sentry and PostHog. No ad SDK. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (2.10.140, versionCode 320), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).
Not on F-Droid despite an earlier entry claiming so: the F-Droid API answers 404. Play is where the file comes from, so hasSignedIndex is false and the pinned digest is the only remaining defence.

LPG filling stations on a map, with directions handed to Waze or Maps: fuel for the car, so it sits with navigation. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.1.5, versionCode 4113), signed with Play App Signing.

Streams, so it is granted network, and its policy is a four host whitelist rather than an open door. The certificate was read off the installed application and its SHA-1 matches the one KDroidDatabase records for this package exactly, which is as good a confirmation as this catalog can get that the build on the device is the build the policy was written for.

Delek fuelling (Menta). React Native, Google Maps, Firebase, AppsFlyer and Emarsys. No ad SDK. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (8.0.4, versionCode 132), signed with the developer's own key (CN=keeprz, O=keeprz, L=Tel Aviv).

Markdown notes, kept as files on the device. Given no network: it embeds web pages (YouTube, X, Bilibili, Reddit) inside notes and community plugins download code from GitHub and unpkg, and none of that is needed to write notes. Sync and publish will not work. Pin and version from the build installed from Play (1.14.4, versionCode 389), signed with Play App Signing (CN=Android, O=Google Inc.).
Computes its times from the position and the clock, the same arithmetic this product does for its own home screen, so it needs no network. Offline and available in every mode.

Offered in the store and given no network at all, which is what its upstream policy says and what a siddur needs. minUserMode OFFLINE for the same reason: an application that asks for nothing should be available in every mode, including the one where nothing is allowed out.
